items.text: In early counting from Taiwan's [[e:2026 Taiwanese local elections|local elections]], Reuters reported Taipei mayor [[p:Chiang Wan-an]] of the [[p:Kuomintang]] leading the [[p:Democratic Progressive Party|DPP]]'s [[p:Puma Shen]], whom Beijing says is wanted for separatism. The DPP looked on course to hold Kaohsiung and Tainan and the KMT to hold New Taipei, while the DPP's Ho Hsin-chun narrowly led in Taichung. Taiwan's defence ministry counted 33 Chinese military aircraft and eight warships around the island in the 24 hours before voting.
items.notes: PRELIMINARY: the Reuters count is from about 18:00 local time (10:00 UTC); neither Taipei camp had conceded. Final results were expected before midnight and the CEC formally announces winners on 4 Dec. The Focus Taiwan live page (CNA) had no results when fetched. A nuclear-power referendum was held the same day; no result yet. Military-activity figures are from Reuters, Yahoo copy: https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/taiwan-votes-key-local-elections-000134325.html . Last cycle (2022) the KMT won 14, the DPP 5 and others 3. UPDATE WITH FINAL RESULTS.

items.text: [[p:United States Central Command|US Central Command]] said an aircraft fired precision munitions at the stern of the Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman after it left Bandar Abbas and tried to run the US blockade of Iranian ports; the crew was unharmed. AP counts it as at least the 15th ship disabled since April. On 27 Nov the [[p:Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps|IRGC]] said a tanker on an 'unauthorised' route hit a mine and exploded and another turned back, and Iran's navy chief said Iran would break the blockade.
items.notes: The IRGC mine claim is unverified. Press TV placed it north of Ghannam Island (Pakistan Today: https://www.pakistantoday.com.pk/2026/11/27/irgc-says-tanker-hit-mine-exploded-in-strait-of-hormuz); the 28 Nov Al Jazeera blog says two tankers hit mines near Khasab. The IRGC also claimed warning shots at a US F-16 near Hengam Island. The US says it has redirected 158 ships since July.

items.text: Italian Foreign Minister [[p:Antonio Tajani]] said Kuwaiti investigators found the drone that killed two Italian technicians in Kuwait was made in Iran, while noting that Iran's allies also field Iranian-made drones. Iran denies launching it; Foreign Minister [[p:Abbas Araghchi]] called the attack suspicious, and Tehran has offered to join a joint inquiry with Italy and Kuwait. Saudi Arabia and Syria blamed Iran.
items.notes: Tajani's statement attributes manufacture, not who launched it. Al Jazeera live blog 28 Nov: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/11/28/iran-war-live-italy-says-drone-in-deadly-kuwait-attack-was-made-in-iran

items.text: [[p:Donald Trump]] publicly backed Iraqi PM Ali al-Zaidi's drive to stop oil smuggling and put all weapons under state control. During the week Baghdad moved to put the Kurdistan Region's border crossings and several oilfields under federal control and closed two crossings, one to Syria and one to Iran. Iraq's top court ruled that federal forces can deploy on all borders, including the Kurdish region's. The [[p:Kurdistan Regional Government]] called this a breach of its constitutional rights but said it does not want clashes, and thousands protested on 26 Nov.
items.notes: No independent second link was fetched (web-search budget exhausted, Rudaw blocked). Al-Zaidi had earlier ordered the army to prepare to enter Jurf al-Sakhar, held by Kataib Hezbollah. A Baghdad–Erbil meeting under the Supreme Judicial Council head is set for 1 Dec. Baghdad estimates it lost about $100bn to smuggling in 2008–25; Reuters says how that figure was calculated is unclear.

items.text: [[p:Médecins Sans Frontières|MSF]] said an Israeli strike directly hit its clearly marked clinic in Gaza City on the night of 27 Nov, killing two staff guards. It said the clinic's location was known to the Israeli military and that 17 of its staff have now been killed in Gaza. The Israeli military said the two were Hamas members but gave no evidence. WHO chief [[p:Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus]] called the strike unacceptable.
items.thread: Gaza ceasefire and Board of Peace plan
items.notes: Al Jazeera dates it to 'Friday' night, which is 27 Nov. Sourced to MSF's post on X; no independent second outlet was fetched (msf.org blocked). On 27 Nov Al Jazeera also reported four killed in Gaza and a strike that the son of Hamas leader al-Hayya survived.

items.text: National Assembly head Jorge Rodríguez said Venezuela will repeal the 2024 law used to bar opposition figures who backed sanctions from holding office, one of the laws flagged for review in the US-backed transition talks. [[p:María Corina Machado]], who was excluded from the talks, launched neighbourhood assemblies to draft a government programme. Her team said about 2,000 met on day one. No election date has been set.
items.notes: The repeal's timing and mechanism were not given. Repeal would remove a legal bar Machado faced. No independent second link was fetched.
